manifest.description: Method Object pattern — extract a method into a standalone class with private final fields for the parameters, a constructor, and an execute() method. Original method becomes a thin delegate.
when_to_use: split a god-method as the first step toward extracting private helpers — once the body lives in a fresh class, intra-method extracts get cleaner scopes
introduce a Method Object before chaining java-extract-code-block to break the body into private helpers
isolate a method for stand-alone unit testing without dragging the enclosing class along
anti_patterns: do not use on static methods — Method Object is an instance-method pattern; use a static factory class refactor instead
do not use on methods that mutate enclosing fields — planner refuses with mutated_enclosing_field; refactor to return the new value instead
do not use on methods that call other enclosing-class methods receiverlessly — planner refuses; inline helpers first (java-inline-method) or thread them as params
do not use on constructors — that needs a separate factory-class refactor

module_name.description: Name of the method to convert.

target.description: Path for the new class file. Must not exist.

new_text.description: Optional new class name (PascalCase). Default: PascalCase of method name + 'Operation' (e.g. processOrder → ProcessOrderOperation).

impl_name.description: Optional enclosing class name when source has multiple classes.

target_prelude.description: Optional prefix for the new file. Defaults to source's package + imports.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-convert-method-to-class. Charter: Extract a method body into a standalone Method Object class.

Protocol:

1. Ground structurally:
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")

2. Confirm the method is convertible:
   - not static, not abstract, not a constructor
   - body does not depend on enclosing fields (or operator has already lifted those to parameters)

3. Plan with deep_analysis=true:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="convert_method_to_class",
                      deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{source}}",
                      module_name="{{module_name}}",
                      target="{{target}}",
                      new_text="{{new_text}}",
                      impl_name="{{impl_name}}",
                      target_prelude="{{target_prelude}}")

   Planner emits two FileEdits: write the new class file, replace the
   original method body with `return new <Class>(<args>).execute();`.
   The class has a constructor that accepts every original parameter
   and stores them as private final fields; execute() carries the
   method's original body verbatim, including the throws clause.

   If the body uses this/super, the planner inserts a FIXME comment
   inside execute() and counts the references in fixme_count.warning.
   Address those before applying, or accept that the generated class
   won't compile and fix it after.

4. Apply:
   bbox_refactor_apply(plan_path="<plan_path>", confirm=true)

5. Compile-verify with the project's build.

6. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line summary: class name, parameter count, fixme count>).

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never apply with fixme_count.warning > 0 unless you understand each this/super reference and intend to hand-edit the generated class to thread an enclosing-instance argument.
- Never use this for static utility methods — convert the class to instance form first if needed, or pick a different refactor.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{source}} {{module_name}} {{target}} {{new_text}} {{impl_name}} {{target_prelude}}
